title: Ray–Singer and dynamical Milnor metric comparison for Morse–Smale flows with untwisted closed orbits on closed connected orientable manifolds
source_title: Morse-Smale flow, Milnor metric, and dynamical zeta function
author: Shu Shen; Jianqing Yu
difficulty_reason: The cited Franks standardisation and Bismut--Zhang theorem do not by themselves compare the dynamical Milnor metric with the analytic metric for the original Morse--Smale flow. The author constructs the untwisted determinant-line fusion comparison through orbit destruction and proves the matching variation of the characteristic current. Tracking those metric and current contributions, including the negative-vector-field sign, is the nonroutine step that makes the final comparison formula hold.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem3.12 restricted to closed connected orientable smooth X and Morse–Smale flows whose closed orbits all have orientable unstable bundles. Thus every closed orbit is Case1, for which the new comparison proof is written in full, avoiding the explicitly omitted nonorientable/twisted extensions in2.6–2.10 and3.5. Complex flat bundle and arbitrary Hermitian metric, without acyclicity or unitarity assumptions; all determinant-line metrics and the negative-vector-field sign are retained. Original Franks standardization/orbit-destruction theorem in its orientable case and Bismut–Zhang analytic torsion theorem are explicit named prior research foundations. Fusion diagram and characteristic-current variation are complete. Bounded display note:3.21 last term prints minus V, whereas its preceding sentence replaces minus V by gradient f and the immediately following3.22 displays the intended gradient-f term; no additional current calculation is supplied by us.
